title: Base change of an ell-adic inverse-limit tower and of its finite reduction tensor
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a scheme morphism $h:T'\to T$, the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and their inverse-image functor [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Write $R_T=(\mathbf Z_\ell)_T$, with constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and coefficient ring [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. Let $(F_{r,T},t_{r,T})_{r\geq1}$ and $(F_{r,T'},t_{r,T'})_{r\geq1}$ be towers of $R_T$- and $R_{T'}$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], respectively, with $\ell^rF_{r,S}=0$. Let $L_S=\varprojlim_r F_{r,S}$ with projections $p_{r,S}$ [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Assume that the canonical ring-sheaf maps $h^{-1}(\Lambda)_T\to(\Lambda)_{T'}$ of constant sheaves are isomorphisms for $\Lambda=\mathbf Z_\ell$ (and, in the second part, for $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^N$ and $A$), and regard inverse images of modules as modules over the target constant rings through them. Suppose $R_{T'}$-linear isomorphisms $\beta_{r,h}:h^{-1}F_{r,T}\to F_{r,T'}$ commute with transitions. Then there is a unique $R_{T'}$-linear map
$$c_h:h^{-1}L_T\to L_{T'},\qquad p_{r,T'}c_h=\beta_{r,h}h^{-1}p_{r,T}.$$
If such tower comparisons are given for identity and composable morphisms and obey their identity/composition laws, the $c_h$ obey the same laws, under the canonical inverse-image composition identifications.

Let $A$ be a commutative $\mathbf Z_\ell$-algebra killed by $\ell^N$, $N\geq1$, and let $Q_S=(\mathbf Z/\ell^N)_S$. Form sheaf tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], put $B_S=L_S\otimes_{R_S}A_S$ and $D_S=F_{N,S}\otimes_{Q_S}A_S$, and define $\alpha_S:B_S\to D_S$ by $x\otimes a\mapsto p_{N,S}(x)\otimes a$. Under the canonical tensor pullback identifications, $b_h=c_h\otimes1:h^{-1}B_T\to B_{T'}$ and $d_h=\beta_{N,h}\otimes1:h^{-1}D_T\to D_{T'}$ satisfy
$$\alpha_{T'}b_h=d_hh^{-1}\alpha_T.$$
The $b_h$ obey identity and composition laws. If $\alpha_T$ and $\alpha_{T'}$ are isomorphisms, then $b_h$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Construct the scalar-extension Hom equivalence by the sectionwise extend/restrict-scalars adjunction and module sheafification. Its value on a pure tensor is a times the value on 1 tensor x. Naturality of toSheafify makes the constant coefficient maps commute with direct image. Combine the scalar-extension equivalence, the inverse-image adjunction, and the resulting identity-on-sections direct-scalar isomorphism to obtain tensorPullbackHomEquiv. Its value on adjunction units proves existence and uniqueness of tateTensorMap. Yoneda and these equivalences show that this map is invertible whenever the supplied module map is.

proof.text: For a surjective coefficient homomorphism q, the induced map of constant ring sheaves is locally surjective. Mathlib restrictHomEquivOfIsLocallySurjective therefore identifies maps before and after scalar restriction. Construct the quotient action on the unchanged underlying abelian sheaf by factoring its scalar representation through q, and extend the action from the constant presheaf via PresheafOfModules.sheafify. The old and new restricted actions agree by the sheafification scalar equation, giving the presentation. For p-adic reduction, ker_toZModPow and the level annihilation hypothesis supply the required kernel condition. Full faithfulness of scalar restriction proves uniqueness up to the unique compatible isomorphism. Separately factor the algebra map using RingHom.liftOfSurjective; its kernel condition follows from l^(n+1)=0 in A.

proof.text: Combine scalar-restriction full faithfulness, the inverse-image adjunctions and the direct-scalar isomorphism to lift the finite-level R-linear isomorphism to Q coefficients. Its unit formula is the specified finite tensor formula. Yoneda reflects invertibility through this Hom equivalence, and tensorMap_isIso gives invertibility after tensoring.

proof.text: Apply tensorPullbackHomEquiv and injectivity of the inverse-image adjunction to test the finite square on units of 1 tensor x. The tensor-map and reduction formulas reduce its two sides to the limit projection equation; cancel the finite presentation isomorphisms. If both reduction maps are invertible, the square and invertibility of the finite tensor map imply invertibility of the limit tensor map. Specialize to the unique quotient presentations and algebra map for the canonical square.

proof.text: For identity pullback, identify direct image with the identity using site pullbackId and constant-sheaf unit naturality. Take the adjoint mate of this identification; the mate unit equation proves the required identity normalization and adjunction injectivity proves uniqueness. For composition retain the existing exchangeModuleComposition and the canonical equality proEtaleConstantRingCompositeCoefficients_eq. Its prescribed conjugate and the adjunction mate unit equation give the iterated-unit formula for this same compositor.

proof.text: Limit identity and composition follow from the projection equations and naturality of the retained canonical comparisons. Tensor identity follows from its unique pure-tensor normalization. Tensor composition is checked on units of 1 tensor x using tensorPullbackHomEquiv injectivity: the compositor unit formula, naturality, and the pure-tensor formulas give identical iterated images. This proves the laws for the b maps with the same canonical compositor.
